result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.min_weighted_dominating_set()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find an approximate minimum weighted dominating set. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L27542-L27639){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.min_weighted_dominating_set(weight_attr=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Minimum weighted dominating set](/assets/graphs/min-weighted-dominating-set.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The same seven-node graph, with each node's weight w in a badge: the hubs 2 and 5 cost 4, every other node costs 1. The cheapest dominating set found is 1, 4, and 6 (accent), with an accent edge from each other node to the member that dominates it. The card shows [1, 4, 6] and total weight 1 + 1 + 1 = 3." width="100%"} Uses a greedy algorithm that iteratively adds the most cost-effective node (lowest weight per number of newly dominated nodes) to the dominating set. This provides an `O(log n)` approximation to the optimal solution. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [weight_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional node attribute name to use as weights. If `None` or the attribute doesn't exist on a node, the node is assumed to have weight `1`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of node IDs forming an approximate minimum weighted dominating set. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Implements the Chvátal-style greedy heuristic that at each step picks the node maximizing *domination gain per unit weight*: newly dominated nodes divided by the candidate's weight. Running this to completion in $O(V \cdot E)$ time produces a dominating set whose total weight is within an $O(\log n)$ factor of optimal, a bound that matches the best possible polynomial-time approximation ratio for the weighted set-cover problem it generalizes. Nodes with a missing or unrecognized `weight_attr=` attribute are treated as weight $1$, and the unweighted case (every weight equal to $1$) degenerates to `dominating_set()`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} The hub costs far more than any leaf, so the weighted algorithm favors dominating via the cheaper leaves where possible, factoring in node cost rather than just node count: ::: {#06c8f021 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="hub", cost=10) .add_node(label="leaf1", cost=1) .add_node(label="leaf2", cost=1) .add_node(label="leaf3", cost=1) .add_edge("hub", "leaf1") .add_edge("hub", "leaf2") .add_edge("hub", "leaf3") ) dom = graph.min_weighted_dominating_set(weight_attr="cost") # Returns the labels chosen to minimize total cost [graph.get_label_from_id(n) for n in dom] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['leaf1', 'leaf2', 'leaf3'] ``` ::: ::: This generalizes to a facility-location-style problem: place facilities at low-cost nodes such that every node in the grid is covered: ::: {#f53a16db .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import random graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_grid_2d(rows=5, cols=5) random.seed(23) node_ids = graph.get_node_ids() costs = {nid: random.uniform(1, 10) for nid in node_ids} graph.set_node_attrs("facility_cost", costs) facilities = graph.min_weighted_dominating_set(weight_attr="facility_cost") # Returns the number of facilities needed to cover the entire grid len(facilities) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 8 ``` ::: :::
